title: Sunday's boring SaaS, 1 November 2026
dek: Sunday, 1 November 2026. Obscreen and a newer Conductor number are Stripe-verified. The other ten are self-reported. Several of those interviews are a few years old, so the number is from that date.

companies.name: TitleCapture
companies.description: Each US title company gets its own white-label app. Its real-estate agents and lenders use it to make title quotes, seller net sheets, and buyer estimates without calling a title rep. Miami. Started October 2013.
companies.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story, 20 November 2023. Not independently checked. "$300K+ MRR (close to $4m ARR)". The page header says $333K of revenue a month, 2 founders, and 35 employees. More than 1,500 title companies, "close to 10% of the entire title company market." Around 30% profitability, and they have never taken funding. About $300 a month per title company.
companies.indieAngle: A back-office industry where the customer gives your tool to its own customers.
companies.whyItPrints: A title company hands "their app" to its agents. The founder says churn is very low, because taking the app back is hard. The fee is about $300 a month. One industry partnership took them from 1 customer to more than 150 in the first year.

companies.name: Data Fetcher
companies.description: An Airtable extension that imports data from REST APIs, Stripe, Google Search Console, and other ready-made sources into Airtable on a schedule, without code. Solo founder Andy Cloke, London. Started August 2020.
companies.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story. Not independently checked. The 2022 interview says 190 paying customers and $6,500 a month. The 2024 update says $23,000 a month, growing from $6,000 to $23,000, with churn down to 7%. The goal is 1,000 customers and $500,000 a year. The page header says $23K of revenue a month, 1 founder, and 0 employees.
companies.indieAngle: A solo founder became the default importer inside one product, and that product can change the rules.
companies.whyItPrints: Operations people pay so they do not have to write a script between Airtable and the other system. The founder names the risk himself: Airtable pricing and platform changes.

companies.name: Sync2Sheets
companies.description: A Google Workspace add-on that syncs Notion databases into Google Sheets for reporting, formulas, and charts. Solo founder Leandro Zubrezki, Buenos Aires. Started May 2021. He also builds Coda integrations.
companies.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story, 7 May 2024. Not independently checked. $9,000 a month, with more than 400 paying customers. The page header says $9K of revenue a month, 1 founder, and 0 employees. Costs are about $500 a month. LTV is about $300. Churn is about 7%.
companies.indieAngle: Two tools people already live in, and a paid sync between them.
companies.whyItPrints: People pay for a spreadsheet export. The interview says customers run from small businesses to Canva and Wix. Switching from a free plan to paid-only, with a trial, took him from about 15 to more than 40 new paying customers a month.

companies.name: TextMagic
companies.description: A web app and an API for a business to send and receive SMS: reminders, notifications, campaigns, surveys, and a Zapier integration. Most features came from support tickets. Tallinn. CEO Priit Vaikmaa. Founded 2001.
companies.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story, 21 June 2022. Not independently checked. "Our revenue in 2021 was just short of €11 million." The page header says $1.2M of revenue a month and 51 employees. Those two figures are both on the page. This interview is from 2022, so the number is 2021, not today.
companies.indieAngle: A 20-year-old SMS business. A smaller version is texting for one trade.
companies.whyItPrints: The company bills for every message. The CEO says they never really had to convince people that a text was an easier way to reach a customer.

companies.name: Diesel Laptops
companies.description: Diagnostic kits for truck and off-highway mechanics: a laptop, software, and cables, plus repair information, its own software, and tech support. Sold to repair shops and fleets. It started as eBay bundles in 2012. Irmo, South Carolina.
companies.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story, 18 December 2018. Not independently checked. Sales were $3.5 million in 2015, almost $8 million in 2016, and $16 million in 2017. The page headline says $20 million a year, and the header says $4.2 million of revenue a month and 180 employees. Those header figures are as shown on the page, not the 2017 sales line. Over $1 million that year on paid search. Profitable, with every penny reinvested. This is a 2018 interview.
companies.indieAngle: The hardware kit is the sale. The software and the repair data on top of it are the part that can recur.
companies.whyItPrints: Shops pay $2,000 to $8,000 or more for a tool that saves technician hours. Support and updates are why they keep buying. Leads come from paid search at about $50 for a high-quality lead, and most sales close by phone.

companies.name: DASHP
companies.description: It started as commission and performance tracking for door-to-door pest-control sales teams. The site now pitches a fuller pest-control platform, with technicians, routing, and field sales. Solo founder Isaac Z Tai. Started October 2022. US.
companies.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story, 17 December 2024. Not independently checked. "Just over 100k ARR." The page header says $8,333 of revenue a month, 1 founder, and 0 employees. The stack moved from Retool to Expo and Supabase.
companies.indieAngle: One trade, one spreadsheet, and a yearly seat.
companies.whyItPrints: Commission spreadsheets in a seasonal door-to-door trade. Seats come with a 12-month commitment. Month-to-month flex seats cost twice as much and are capped at 30% of seats. Standard seats are $10 to $30 a month. No funding.

companies.name: Stagetimer
companies.description: A browser countdown for a stage. The producer controls it remotely, and speakers see the time left on any screen. Lukas Hermann and Liz, Stuttgart. Started November 2021.
companies.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story. Not independently checked. The interview of 6 January 2023 says $8,000 in monthly revenue on average. The page header now shows $25K of revenue a month, 2 founders, and 0 employees. That header figure is not explained in the story text. Both numbers stay.
companies.indieAngle: A crew will pay for one reliable screen backstage.
companies.whyItPrints: One job, a clock, for conference crews. Growth came from Reddit, search, and word of mouth. Customers buy 2 to 6 licenses a year.

companies.name: MySignature
companies.description: An HTML email-signature builder for a person or a team. It started in 2015 and was acquired in 2019 by Vol Zastavny's company Solva. The team is of Ukrainian origin.
companies.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story, 11 January 2024. Not independently checked. Almost $700,000 a year, fully bootstrapped, 500,000-plus users, about half of Solva's revenue. The page header says $55K of revenue a month.
companies.indieAngle: They bought a tool that already existed, then worked on search and the signup.
companies.whyItPrints: A signature at the bottom of an email. The interview treats search and the Gmail integration as the way people find it.

companies.name: CraftMyPDF
companies.description: A drag-and-drop template editor, plus an API and Zapier and Make, that turns JSON into invoices, certificates, labels, and reports as PDFs. Solo founder Jacky Tan, Singapore. Started November 2020, using a $300 boilerplate.
companies.evidence: Self-reported, Starter Story, 4 April 2023. Not independently checked. $15,000 a month for both products combined. The page header says $15K of revenue a month, 1 founder, and 1 employee. More than 2 million PDF documents and images generated over two years. The interview does not name the second product.
companies.indieAngle: An API for a document a developer would rather rent than keep running.
companies.whyItPrints: A back office needs a document made from data. Growth came from search after ads did not work. Churn is mostly customers who no longer needed the service.

companies.name: Obscreen
companies.description: Digital signage. It organises media and plays it on a TV, a computer, a tablet, or any browser, in the cloud or self-hosted. Restaurants, retail, logistics, gyms, hospitals, and offices. One person. Founded September 2024. Bootstrapped. The profile says it is used in 30-plus countries. France.
companies.evidence: MRR $482. 26 subscriptions. Last 30 days $395. All-time $15,388. Last-30-day margin 80% claimed. Listed for sale at $25,000. Revenue synced 1 November 2026 ~07:57 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Signage money is usually a price per screen for a business with more than one location. This listing is the small end of that.
companies.whyItPrints: Menu boards and lobby screens. A self-host option is how it gets around. The listing is for sale.

companies.name: ScreenshotOne
companies.description: A screenshot, PDF, and video API. Solo founder Dmytro Krasun. Pricing is subscriptions plus pay-as-you-go. No funding. A target of $50,000 a month is a goal, not a current figure.
companies.evidence: Self-reported. Not independently checked. A late-September brief put it near $12,000 a month, from Starter Story. That note is not on this site. Indie Hackers, 5 March 2026, says over 800 paying customers and over $25,000 a month. SoloBiz, 27 October 2026, repeats more than $25,000 a month and more than 800 customers. The $25,000 figure is from March 2026, so it is not necessarily today's number.
companies.indieAngle: An unsexy API that is easier to rent than to maintain.
companies.whyItPrints: Developers pay so they do not have to keep a screenshot service running themselves.

companies.name: Conductor
companies.description: The QuickBooks Desktop and Enterprise API. $49 per company file per month to read and write the file over REST, Python, or Node, instead of the Web Connector and qbXML (founder-stated). Founder Danny Nemer, US, founded July 2022. The 1 November listing is still for sale. The monthly Stripe line is a bit higher than the 30 October note, and the last 30 days are a bit lower.
companies.evidence: MRR $45,770. 305 subscriptions. Last 30 days $43,642. All-time $505,682. Last-30-day margin 95% claimed. Still listed for sale at $1,250,000. Revenue synced 1 November 2026 ~09:24 Warsaw. The 30 October note was MRR $45,524, 302 subscriptions, last 30 days $44,395, and all-time $504,399.
companies.indieAngle: Same QuickBooks Desktop API as the earlier notes. The monthly Stripe line moved up a little, the last 30 days moved down a little, and it is still for sale.
companies.whyItPrints: Developers still pay so QuickBooks Desktop behaves like a normal API. The monthly line is a little higher, the last 30 days are a little lower, and the listing is still for sale.
